dataset.points: 75 % Gaussian clusters (sigma 40 km) around 10 cities, 25 % uniform in the bbox

queries.filter_ge_numeric_properties: the same on the GeoJSON-loaded engine (numbers)
queries.filter_by_polygon_buffer: filter_by_polygon(buffer((19.076, 72.8777), 50.0)): tested as an exact circle
queries.filter_by_polygon_buffer_as_plain_polygo: the same 64-gon ring as a plain Polygon (ray casting)
queries.operations run on: the engine loaded from CSV with default options (string values); the CSV- and GeoJSON-loaded engines are both in memory while the non-load operations run, the three loads run with neither

notes: Timing numbers are indicative: this run shared a 4-CPU machine with other jobs.

Dataset operations: median and min of repeats, each repeat a calibrated loop after a gc.collect(). 'operations' has the garbage collector on; 'operations_gc_disabled' comes from loops with it off, alternating with the on loops.
Per-call micro-benchmarks run with the garbage collector off, like timeit.
The Python under test differs from the cp312 wheels used for the footprint comparison; wheel sizes do not depend on the interpreter running this script.

micro.note: Per-call loops run with the garbage collector off, like timeit. Every scalar callable is wrapped in the same kind of lambda; the empty-lambda row is that shared overhead and is not subtracted. Vectorized rows exclude building the numpy arrays.

import_time._method: Median of 2 fresh interpreter processes per statement, in shuffled order. importtime_cumulative_ms sums the top-level cumulative times that python -X importtime reports for modules not already loaded by an empty interpreter. .pyc files exist and the OS file cache is warm, so this is a cold interpreter, not a cold disk. qoregeo is an editable install (a .pth path entry), so its import reads the repository source tree.

memory_load._method: Each case runs in a fresh interpreter after qoregeo is imported. tracemalloc counts Python allocations only; peak is the high-water mark during the load, current is what the loaded object keeps. rss_growth and peak_rss_growth come from /proc/self/status (VmRSS, VmHWM) in a second, untraced run (Linux only); they include allocator overhead and memory the allocator keeps.
